raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Pi0.5 currently transfers and encodes every configured camera, including views masked out for the entire batch. Add an opt-in way to skip that work. The default remains unchanged because different vision batches, prefix lengths, and attention paths can change floating-point outputs.

## Modifications

- Add `drop_masked_cameras=False` to the Pi0.5 pipeline config.
- Use the same filtered camera order for prefix encoding and cache keys. Remove only views with an all-false CPU mask; retain mixed-validity views, non-CPU masks, and the original layout when every view would be removed.
- Add seven focused regressions for configuration, batch masks, cache keys, graph layout, fallback, and effective positions; document the numerical behavior in the existing cookbook.

## Accuracy Tests

The four Python files are byte-identical to the patch evaluated on base `5007cbd6a57515bf5e008ff2fd2bdb834356b53c`. That campaign completed 20,000 LIBERO episodes: 6,000 per A/B arm plus 4,000 episodes for each of two A/A controls. The full campaign was not rerun on the rebased candidate.

| Suite | Flag off | Flag on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Spatial | 1477/1500 | 1483/1500 |
| Object | 1470/1500 | 1475/1500 |
| Goal | 1470/1500 | 1465/1500 |
| LIBERO-10 | 1372/1500 | 1384/1500 |
| Total | 5789/6000 (96.4833%) | 5807/6000 (96.7833%) |

The paired result is +0.3000 percentage points, with 88 baseline-only and 106 candidate-only successes. A suite-stratified task bootstrap gives a 95% interval of [-0.0167, +0.6000] percentage points; no noninferiority margin was prespecified. A/A used policy seed 7 only: baseline 1922→1921/2000 and candidate 1925→1926/2000. Exact pixel hashes were diagnostic under an outcome-blind audit amendment: all three campaigns failed the original exact-pixel gate, and three historical post-run package snapshots are missing. These results describe this configuration; they do not prove numerical equivalence or noninferiority.

Configuration: OpenPI-converted LIBERO checkpoint SHA256 `0046d3a3a6b38a8ced3fcdf85afc980c9fe37c1bddd720a087ac09ab1b595cc0`; horizon 10, internal action dim 32/output dim 7, 10 denoise steps, replan every 5 actions, plain instruction without discrete state tokens, environment seed 7, policy seeds 7/17/27, 40 tasks × 50 initial states per seed. This is not the canonical LeRobot horizon-50 evaluation.

On the rebased candidate at `03aba9e6479788470750b884333f20cc270e06f6`, a fresh real-weight check passed for both flags in eager and CUDA Graph modes, including prefix/action capture and replay. Each fixed observation/noise repeated three times identically within its arm; eager and graph outputs matched within each flag. Between flags, the largest absolute difference in the final 10×7 actions was 0.0012294352 for that input.

On the rebased candidate, 75 selected native unit tests passed (including all seven new regressions), with no failures or skips, in the compatibility runtime below. Cookbook configuration checks and 52 documentation-script tests passed. Focused pre-commit passed for all five changed files. Full repository CI and Mint link/build checks remain pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fresh same-GPU comparison on base `03aba9e…`, with both prefix and action graphs enabled, batch 1, three configured cameras/one fully masked, horizon 10 and 10 denoise steps. Each arm ran in a fresh process with 10 warmups and 30 measured requests; global prefix cache was disabled.

| Metric | Flag off | Flag on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Physical prefix tokens | 777 | 521 |
| Mean model invocation | 59.9966 ms | 42.9002 ms |

Timing covers prefix encoding, action sampling, and the CPU action copy; it excludes HTTP decoding, image preprocessing, and action unnormalization. Latency decreased by 28.50% (1.3985×). This includes existing attention-path changes enabled by a fully valid remaining prefix; it is not a robot-loop speedup or per-kernel attribution. No memory saving is claimed.

Runtime: NVIDIA RPBZZZ6 (SM120, 96 GB), driver 580.159.04, Python 3.10.20, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu128, Transformers 5.12.1, `torch_sdpa`, BF16 backbone with existing FP32 stability compute. This compatibility runtime differs from current upstream pins, including its Python >=3.11 requirement; these are not upstream CI results.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the changed files with project pre-commit hooks.
- [x] Add focused unit tests.
- [x] Update the existing Pi0.5 documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results with configuration and scope.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

Request CODEOWNERS review and maintainer-triggered CI; merge after required approvals and green CI.

 ## 5. Configuration Tips
 
 - Request-local `PrefixContext` is always reused across all denoise steps in one request. The prefix K/V is not cloned per step.
+- `drop_masked_cameras` is disabled by default. Set it to `true` in your pipeline config to skip views whose CPU mask is false for every batch item before image transfer and encoding. Views with any valid batch item or a non-CPU mask are kept; if all views would be removed, the original camera layout is kept. Pruning changes vision batches, physical prefix length, reduction shapes, and attention execution paths, so outputs need not be bit-exact. Validate closed-loop quality for your checkpoint and configuration before enabling it.
 - The optional global prefix cache is a bounded exact-match LRU. It is disabled by default because changing robot frames rarely hit it and enabling it prevents unrelated misses from entering grouped prefix execution. Set `enable_global_prefix_cache=true` for repeated observations, retries, or multiple policy calls over the same camera/state sample; `runtime.prefix_cache` can then disable lookup per request.
 - Partial-prefix reuse is not supported because Pi0.5 combines image and tokenized task/state inputs under full attention. Changing any input can change every deeper-layer prefix K/V tensor. The exact key hashes resized and normalized pixels before SigLIP, plus effective token IDs, token masks, camera masks, model revision, dtype, and parallel layout. Tensor content hashing reuses SRT's CPU/CUDA implementation; hashing the pre-SigLIP input lets an exact hit skip both the vision encoder and prefix transformer.
 - CUDA graph capture targets single-request prefix encoding and one action-denoise step. The lossless default keeps exact prompt lengths and one resident prefix graph. Prefix and action graph residency are independently bounded by `prefix_cuda_graph_max_entries` (default `1`) and `action_cuda_graph_max_entries` (default `4`). Without prompt buckets, unseen signatures run eagerly after the cache reaches capacity, avoiding capture churn. The denoise signature includes whether prefix attention is full or masked, plus batch size, prefix length, action horizon, action dim, dtype, and parallel layout. Mask-aware action graphs rebuild position IDs from the current request mask inside the captured graph. With action SP enabled, the denoise bucket uses the local action shard length and rank-specific position offset.
-- `prompt_token_buckets` optionally right-pads prompt tokens to fixed sizes such as `[32, 64, 128, 200]`, allowing nearby prompt lengths to reuse both graphs. In this mode the bounded graph caches use LRU replacement and reset evicted CUDA graphs; prompts beyond the largest configured bucket stay exact-length and eager. This is opt-in because padding changes GPU reduction shapes: an H200 sweep over lengths around all four boundaries was structurally correct and bounded to four prefix/action graphs, but non-boundary prompts differed from the exact-length path by up to `0.09589` in normalized action space over five denoise steps. Validate closed-loop policy quality before enabling it; empty buckets preserve the numerically lossless path.
+- `prompt_token_buckets` optionally right-pads prompt tokens to fixed sizes such as `[32, 64, 128, 200]`, allowing nearby prompt lengths to reuse both graphs. In this mode the bounded graph caches use LRU replacement and reset evicted CUDA graphs; prompts beyond the largest configured bucket stay exact-length and eager. This is opt-in because padding changes GPU reduction shapes: an H200 sweep over lengths around all four boundaries was structurally correct and bounded to four prefix/action graphs, but non-boundary prompts differed from the exact-length path by up to `0.09589` in normalized action space over five denoise steps. Validate closed-loop policy quality before enabling it; empty buckets with `drop_masked_cameras=false` preserve the numerically lossless path.
 
 An opt-in four-bucket serving config is:

 | OpenPI/SGLang precision | Official OpenPI JAX inference restores the public GCS checkpoint as bf16 with selected fp32 stability compute and returns float32 actions. The converted OpenPI PyTorch `pi05_aloha` checkpoint keeps `119,720,608` fp32 stability params; SGLang reports the same fp32 set and `3,233,713,264` bf16 runtime params after skipping unused LM heads. |
 | Native attention dtype | Checkpoint source tensors may be fp32, but SGLang finalizes PiGemma and SigLIP compute dtype before native attention backend selection; backend logs showed `Using fa attention backend` for the PiGemma path in the prior run. |
 | 16GB-free Python pressure | With an H100 artificially constrained to `16381 MiB` free before model load, single-GPU bf16 no-offload Python grouped path completed without OOM. Re-run latency after precision or loader changes before using pressure numbers for deployment sizing. |
-| Low-VRAM switches | Disabling prefix cache prevents cache growth across changing robot frames. Prefix graph residency defaults to `1`, action graph residency defaults to `4`, and setting either limit to `0` disables that runner. One validated ALOHA prefix graph used about `48.5 MiB`; action graph residency is now bounded separately. Keep `prompt_token_buckets` empty for the lossless path. |
+| Low-VRAM switches | Disabling prefix cache prevents cache growth across changing robot frames. On 80GB H100, ALOHA OpenPI PyTorch eager was about `125-130 ms` single and about `164 ms / 4` in the direct-model batch path. Current SGLang Python grouped measured `52.4 ms` single and `91.9 ms / 4`; JAX OpenPI was `53.0 ms` single and `59.5 ms / 2` in a short check. |

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    import torch
+
+
+def prune_fully_masked_cameras(
+    camera_order: tuple[str, ...],
+    image_masks: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor],
+) -> tuple[str, ...]:
+    kept = tuple(
+        name
+        for name in camera_order
+        if image_masks[name].device.type != "cpu"
+        or bool(image_masks[name].any().item())
+    )
+    # The vision encoder requires at least one camera. Keep its existing
+    # all-masked behavior rather than introducing a new text-only path.

     return model
 
 
+def _observation_with_camera_masks(masks) -> VLAObservationBatch:
+    observation = _observation_with_token_len(9)
+    observation.images = {
+        name: torch.zeros(1, 3, 4, 4) for name in ("front", "empty", "wrist")
+    }
+    observation.image_masks = {
+        name: torch.tensor([present], dtype=torch.bool)
+        for name, present in zip(observation.images, masks, strict=True)
+    }
+    observation.metadata["camera_order"] = tuple(observation.images)
+    return observation

+def test_masked_camera_pruning_is_opt_in_and_preserves_camera_protocol():
+    observation = _observation_with_camera_masks((True, False, True))
+    baseline = _recording_policy(Pi05PipelineConfig())
+    optimized = _recording_policy(Pi05PipelineConfig(drop_masked_cameras=True))
+
+    baseline_signature = baseline.encode_prefix(observation)
+    optimized_signature = optimized.encode_prefix(observation)
+
+    assert baseline_signature.static_layout[0] == 3
+    assert optimized_signature.static_layout[0] == 2
+    assert baseline_signature != optimized_signature
+    assert optimized_signature.static_layout[1] is True
+    assert tuple(observation.images) == ("front", "empty", "wrist")
+    assert observation.metadata["camera_order"] == ("front", "empty", "wrist")
+    assert optimized.config.image_keys == baseline.config.image_keys
+
+
+def test_masked_camera_presence_change_gets_a_different_graph_signature():
+    optimized = _recording_policy(Pi05PipelineConfig(drop_masked_cameras=True))
+
+    missing = optimized.encode_prefix(
+        _observation_with_camera_masks((True, False, True))
+    )
+    present = optimized.encode_prefix(
+        _observation_with_camera_masks((True, True, True))
+    )
+
+    assert missing != present
+    assert (missing.static_layout[0], present.static_layout[0]) == (2, 3)
+
+
+def test_masked_camera_pruning_changes_the_prefix_cache_layout_key():
+    observation = _observation_with_camera_masks((True, False, True))
+    baseline = _recording_policy(Pi05PipelineConfig())
+    optimized = _recording_policy(Pi05PipelineConfig(drop_masked_cameras=True))
+    for model in (baseline, optimized):
+        model.dtype = torch.bfloat16
+        model.model_path = "lerobot/pi05_libero_base"
+
+    assert baseline.build_prefix_cache_key(
+        observation
+    ) != optimized.build_prefix_cache_key(observation)
+
+
+def test_camera_pruning_keeps_mixed_batch_masks_and_camera_order():
+    masks = {
+        "front": torch.tensor([True, True]),
+        "empty": torch.tensor([False, False]),
+        "wrist": torch.tensor([False, True]),
+    }
+
+    assert prune_fully_masked_cameras(tuple(masks), masks) == ("front", "wrist")
+
+
+def test_camera_pruning_preserves_the_all_masked_fallback():
+    masks = {name: torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.bool) for name in ("front", "wrist")}
+
+    assert prune_fully_masked_cameras(tuple(masks), masks) == tuple(masks)
+
+
+def test_camera_pruning_does_not_read_device_mask_values():
+    class UnreadableDeviceMask:
+        device = SimpleNamespace(type="cuda")
+
+        def any(self):
+            pytest.fail("Pruning must not synchronize a device mask to the host")
+
+    masks = {"front": UnreadableDeviceMask(), "empty": torch.tensor([False])}
+
+    assert prune_fully_masked_cameras(tuple(masks), masks) == ("front",)
+
+
+def test_camera_pruning_preserves_effective_positions():
+    camera_masks = {
+        "front": torch.tensor([True, True]),
+        "empty": torch.tensor([False, False]),
+        "wrist": torch.tensor([False, True]),
+    }
+    retained = prune_fully_masked_cameras(tuple(camera_masks), camera_masks)
+    text_masks = torch.tensor([[True, True, False], [True, True, True]])
+    original = torch.cat(
+        [*[mask[:, None].expand(2, 2) for mask in camera_masks.values()], text_masks],
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    pruned = torch.cat(
+        [*[camera_masks[name][:, None].expand(2, 2) for name in retained], text_masks],
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    keep = torch.tensor([0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8])
+
+    assert torch.equal(original.cumsum(1)[:, keep] - 1, pruned.cumsum(1) - 1)
+    assert torch.equal(original.sum(1), pruned.sum(1))
+
+
